findings.evidence: `grep -rn '\.mk\.{' TauCeti` returns only these eight lines; no other file in the repo uses positional `@Struct.mk` with explicit universe annotations. Mathlib's analogue constructs via `⟨X⟩`/`where` (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/AlgCat/Basic.lean:59, TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean:67).
findings.fix: Use structure-instance notation with named fields — `{ blockCount := n, divisionRing := D, degree := d, instDivisionRing := hD, instAlgebra := hKA, instNeZeroDegree := hd, equiv := e }` (instance-implicit fields can be given by name) — and pin universes on the stated return type only, dropping the `.{u, v, u}` annotations on `mk`.
findings.issue: All eight construction sites use positional `@Struct.mk.{…}` with `_` placeholders for the ambient instances (lines 143, 179, 251, 316, 328, 340-341, 355, 369). `blockCount`/`degree` are both `ℕ`-ish and `instDivisionRing`/`instAlgebra`/`instNeZeroDegree` are three adjacent instance fields, so adding or reordering a field silently mis-assigns arguments rather than erroring at the construction site.

findings.evidence: Line 139 `WedderburnPresentation A := by`; lines 143-144 pass `P.instDivisionRing P.instNeZeroDegree` explicitly, so none of the three `letI`s at 140-142 feeds `mk`. `WedderburnPresentation` (line 61) has no `Algebra` field.

findings.issue: `toWedderburnPresentation` is a data-producing `def` written as `by letI …; exact …`, and twelve `rfl`-proved `@[simp]` lemmas (146-166, 215-234, 287-306) depend on it unfolding — which is also why `@[expose]` was needed. Tactic-mode data defs make that unfolding fragile and unreviewable. The `letI : ∀ i, Algebra K (P.divisionRing i)` at line 141 is dead: `WedderburnPresentation.mk` has no algebra field and both instance fields are passed explicitly.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/RingTheory/SimpleModule/Basic.lean:519-520 `noncomputable instance _root_.Module.End.instDivisionRing [DecidableEq (Module.End R M)] [IsSimpleModule R M]`; Mathlib itself hides this behind an existential (`WedderburnArtin.lean:196 `classical exact ⟨n, _, d, inferInstance, …⟩`), whereas here the instance becomes an exposed field.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment: `-- `Module.End.instDivisionRing` needs `DecidableEq (Module.End A (S i))`; the chosen instance is the classical one.` Also drop the redundant `let _` at 249-250 — with the `IsSimpleModule` local in scope, the two `(fun _ ↦ inferInstance)` fields at 255-256 already resolve.
findings.issue: `open Classical in` inside `toWedderburnAlgebraPresentation` is unexplained. It exists to supply `DecidableEq (Module.End A (P.simpleIdeal i))` for `Module.End.instDivisionRing`, which bakes `Classical.decEq` into the exported `divisionRing`/`instDivisionRing` fields of an `@[expose]`d def; a downstream user with a different `DecidableEq` in scope gets a non-syntactically-equal instance. Nothing in the file records this.

findings.evidence: Mathlib's direct analogue is deliberately not simp: Mathlib/Algebra/Category/AlgCat/Basic.lean:59-60 `lemma coe_of (X : Type v) [Ring X] [Algebra R X] : (of R X : Type v) = X := rfl` carries no attribute.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from the five type-valued lemmas, keeping them as plain `theorem`s for explicit `rw`/`exact`. Retain `@[simp]` only on the `blockCount`, `degree`, and `equiv` lemmas.
findings.issue: Five `rfl` lemmas equating `Type`s (or functions into `Type`) are marked `@[simp]`: lines 151-154, 199-203, 220-224, 271-275, 292-296. Rewriting a type with `simp` inside `Matrix _ _ (P.…divisionRing i)` leaves the `DivisionRing`/`Algebra` instance arguments referring to the old type, so these fire as `motive is not type correct` in exactly the goals they are meant to help.

summary: The instance-implicit structure fields are never registered with `attribute [instance]`, forcing manual `letI`/`let _` plumbing at every use site and a `@[simp]` lemma stated under `letI`. Construction goes through eight positional `@Struct.mk.{…}` applications (the only `.mk.{` in the repo), one data `def` is written in tactic mode with a dead `letI`, `open Classical in` is undocumented, and five `rfl` `@[simp]` lemmas equate types.
